finding: src/anomaly/_signal_projection.py:428 Path containment checks are vulnerable to symlink swap races.
rationale: The public build entry point reaches pathname-only checks followed by separate opens and fixed-name staging writes with no lock, private-directory guarantee, no-follow open, directory descriptor, or pinned file handle, so a process able to mutate a shared case can swap an input or staging component after validation and cause out-of-root reads or victim-privileged writes, including writes to canonical evidence, contrary to the locked immutability criterion.

evidence.output: build_signal_projection(root) directly calls build_projection(root); search_signals likewise calls verified_projection(root) and then separately read_rows(projection, ...). There is no upstream lock, case-tree pin, or private-directory guard.

build_projection uses predictable .signals.duckdb.tmp and .signals-manifest.json.tmp names, runs _reset_stage checks, then separately calls duckdb.connect through _write_projection, read_bytes, write_text, and os.replace. verified_projection separately validates paths and later calls read_bytes; _read_projection_inputs similarly returns a checked Path and then calls read_bytes.

_safe_input_file, _prepare_search_root, _existing_search_root, _required_owned_file, _prepare_owned_artifact, and _reset_stage inspect pathnames with is_symlink/is_file/is_dir/resolve/exists and return or continue; none pins an opened object or uses O_NOFOLLOW, openat/dir_fd operations, unique secure staging, locking, or restrictive directory permissions.
The containment test creates the search symlink before build_signal_projection is called and only proves rejection of a pre-existing symlink; it does not cover replacement between validation and use.

The locked acceptance criteria require never modifying canonical data/index.duckdb, evidence/signals.jsonl, or detector-run artifacts, while the security model explicitly supports importing shared cases and rejects links; a post-validation link swap remains within that real shared-case scenario and defeats the required immutability boundary.
